metadata.author: transcribed from live/runs by expansion agent
metadata.key_test: The critical directional-violence test: lethal violence came from the departing higher-P1 power (Indonesia), not the low-P1 fragment. Derives Mod8 (predicts RISK not AGENCY) + Safeguard D for attribution. Also Mod 2 (Safeguard E inversion) for Timor-Leste oil dependence.
metadata.notes: All calls ordinal/directional; no precise MI point scores. East Timor pre-independence WGI reflects UNTAET administration (Safeguard A / Mod 1), not indigenous capacity.

pre_event.event_description: 1999 UN-supervised referendum -> Timor-Leste independence (20 May 2002); the 1999 militia/TNI scorched-earth campaign accompanied the departure of the occupying power.

context.neighbor_details: Indonesia is the former occupier of East Timor (24-year occupation 1975-1999); the departing predatory power in the 1999 violence.
context.growth_trajectory: 1997-98 Asian crisis shock: GDP contracted 13.1% in 1998; rupiah collapsed ~2,400 -> 14,000/USD; Suharto fell May 1998
context.fragmentation_mechanism: loss of occupied territory via referendum

Indonesia.notes: Oil rents ~9.9% of GDP (1998), fell to ~0.8% by 2021. Higher P1 of the pair (a functioning, if crisis-hit, state). Chaotic post-Suharto transition.

context.admin_details: Under UNTAET 1999-2002 (UN administration). Measured P1 = administration, not indigenous capacity (Mod 1).
context.neighbor_details: Indonesia (former occupier); Australia as stabilizing neighbor (INTERFET, led by Maj. Gen. Peter Cosgrove).

East Timor.notes: Economy destroyed - 80% of infrastructure razed in 1999. Near-zero indigenous P1, built from scratch. Petroleum later ~70-80% of GDP; IMF labels it the most oil-dependent economy in the world (Mod 2 / Safeguard E inversion: apparent P4 wealth = vulnerability). Per IMF Country Report No. 25/278: Petroleum Fund balance stood at 939% of non-oil GDP in 2024, but oil/gas production has ceased and continued large withdrawals would deplete it by the end of the 2030s.

a_trajectory_ranking.basis: Indonesia higher P1 despite the 1998 crisis.
a_trajectory_ranking.falsification_condition: East Timor matches or exceeds Indonesia's trajectory.

b_violence.prediction: Low P1 (East Timor) predicts a violent outcome - but the rule does NOT specify who commits the violence; LIVE uses Safeguard D + the directional tag to attribute violence to the departing predatory power (Indonesia).
b_violence.agency_note: Mod8: this predicts RISK, not AGENCY
b_violence.falsification_condition: No violent outcome accompanies the separation.

c_convergence.basis: Wide P1 gap; Indonesia recovers, East Timor undiversified.

d_failure_dimension.note: Most exposed to post-hoc coding bias

e_fragment_count.prediction: 2 successors; Timor-Leste passes the capacity gate only with international scaffolding.
e_fragment_count.falsification_condition: Timor-Leste sustains capacity without external scaffolding, or fragment count differs.

f_reversal_risk.prediction: Timor-Leste reversal / oil-curse risk (Mod 2 inversion; STATIC flags weakly via Safeguard E).
f_reversal_risk.falsification_condition: Timor-Leste durably diversifies and avoids the oil curse.

g_suppression_mechanism.classification: 24 years of Tier 1 military suppression -> 1999 internationally-supervised referendum; a Tier 1 -> exit-via-external-administration shift, not an internal move down the suppression tiers.
g_suppression_mechanism.falsification_condition: Outcome behaves as an internal tier transition rather than an exit.

Indonesia.outcome_summary: Democratized rapidly; GDP grew from ~$95bn (1998) to >$1.3tn (2022); decentralized; remains stable.

East Timor.outcome_summary: Independence 20 May 2002; stable politically but undiversified; 42% poverty; HDI declined after 2010 as oil reserves drew down; oil production has now ceased with Petroleum Fund depletion looming.
key_events: 1999 militia/TNI scorched-earth campaign (violence by departing power)
oil production ceased; fund depletion looming

result_coding_reference.PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED: Direction correct but magnitude, form, or timing significantly different

analysis.overall_assessment: Scored: a CONFIRMED, b PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED (STATIC mis-attribution; LIVE confirmed), c CONFIRMED, f CONFIRMED, g CONFIRMED. The case that most justifies Safeguard D's elevation and the directional violence tag.
safeguards_triggered: Mod8 / directional-violence tag - predicts RISK not AGENCY; derived here to correctly locate the violent actor
Safeguard D - Indonesia as departing predatory power / former occupier (Australia/INTERFET as stabilizer)
Safeguard E (Mod 2 inversion) - Timor-Leste petroleum ~70-80% of GDP, most oil-dependent economy in the world; apparent wealth = vulnerability
Safeguard A (Mod 1) - East Timor measured P1 reflects UNTAET administration, not indigenous capacity
new_failure_modes_discovered: Directional-violence: an unmodified low-P1 -> violence rule mis-locates agency; the departing higher-P1 power was the violent actor. Resolved by Mod8 + Safeguard D.
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: The cleanest demonstration that 'who commits the violence' matters: the departing power, not the low-capacity fragment, was the violent actor. Mod 2's inversion for Timor-Leste is also vindicated - the oil wealth that looks like P4 strength is the central long-run vulnerability.
proposed_framework_modifications: Codify the directional-violence attribution rule (Mod8 / Safeguard D) as a formal amendment to Core Prediction 2; score Case 10 STATIC as a partial falsification on attribution in the master log.
analysis.baseline_impact: Amends Core Prediction 2 (violence risk vs violence agency); LIVE strictly improved accuracy over STATIC.
analysis.phase3_note: Migrated to MI v1 + Data API references. a_trajectory/c_convergence auto-derived from real re-scored data (Mod4-gated); b/d/e/f/g/h preserved as judgment.
